newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf says ends Chevron UK merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Elf says ends Chevron UK merger talks.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine chairman Philippe Jaffre told his group's annual general meeting on Friday that his company had ended negotiations with Chevron about a merger of activities in Britain.
"Following detailed studies, the two parties considered that the planned study would not provide sufficient savings in order to justify the project," an Elf statement said.
These talks were started on November 6, 1996, it said.
"Elf Aquitaine remains determined to optimise its positions in the downstream operations in the U.K. and will pursue its policy of commercial development and productivity improvements," it said.

In March, U.S. Murphy Corp unit Murco decided to exit the proposed merger in favour of going it alone in the highly competitive British petroleum retail sector. But Elf UK Oil and Chevron's Gulf Oil decided to continue their talks.
Britain's refining industry, like most of Europe, has suffered in recent years from a surplus capacity for gasoline production.
A price war among gasoline retailers, initiated at the start of last year by Esso UK in response to the rapid growth of supermarkets as gasoline retailers, has hit profit margins hard.

The three companies, Elf, Chevron and Murco signed a memorandum of understanding in November 1996 to consolidate their refining interests in Milford Haven in south Wales, by ceasing crude processing at the 115,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gulf refinery in Pembroke.
Elf said at the time the merger plans would make a saving of 50 million sterling a year.
